data.definition: A drug used to prevent nausea or vomiting. An antiemetic may act by a wide range of mechanisms: it might affect the medullary control centres (the vomiting centre and the chemoreceptive trigger zone) or affect the peripheral receptors.
data.name: antiemetic

data.definition: A compound formally derived from ammonia by replacing two hydrogen atoms by organyl groups.
data.name: secondary amino compound

data.definition: Drugs capable of inducing illusions, hallucinations, delusions, paranoid ideations and other alterations of mood and thinking.
data.name: hallucinogen

data.definition: Any compound that inhibits one or more steps in the pathway leading to the synthesis of ergosterol.
data.name: ergosterol biosynthesis inhibitor

data.definition: Cyclic hemiacetals formed by intramolecular addition of a hydroxy group to an aldehydic or ketonic carbonyl group. They are thus 1-oxacycloalkan-2-ols or unsaturated analogues.
data.name: lactol

data.definition: The <small>D</small>-enantiomer of ornithine. It is an intermediate metabolite produced in the urea cycle.
data.name: <small>D</small>-ornithine

data.definition: An antiparasitic drug which is effective against Apicomplexan parasites in the genus Plasmodium. The genus contains over 200 species and includes those responsible for malaria.
data.name: antiplasmodial drug

data.definition: Any fluoroarene that is a benzene or a substituted benzene carrying at least one fluoro group.
data.name: fluorobenzenes

data.definition: A Daphnia metabolite produced by the species Daphnia magna.
data.name: Daphnia magna metabolite

data.definition: Any magnesium ion that is positively charged.
data.name: magnesium cation

data.definition: A glycol that is the (S)-enantiomer of 2-methylpentane-2,4-diol.
data.name: (4S)-2-methylpentane-2,4-diol

data.definition: A role played by the molecular entity or part thereof within a chemical context.
data.name: chemical role

data.definition: A α-D-Galp-(1→4)-D-Glcp in which the carbon bearing the anomeric hydroxy group has α configuration.
data.name: α-D-Galp-(1→4)-α-D-Glcp

data.definition: A carboxylic acid containing one or more amino groups.
data.name: amino acid

data.definition: A polar amino acid zwitterion of <small>L</small>-ornithine.
data.name: <small>L</small>-ornithinium(1+)

data.definition: Any constitutionally or isotopically distinct atom, molecule, ion, ion pair, radical, radical ion, complex, conformer etc., identifiable as a separately distinguishable entity.
data.name: molecular entity

data.definition: An inorganic chloride salt having sodium(1+) as the counterion.
data.name: sodium chloride

data.definition: A glycosyl compound resulting from the attachment of a glycosyl group to a non-acyl group RO‒, RS‒, RSe‒, etc. The bond between the glycosyl group and the non-acyl group is called a glycosidic bond. By extension, the terms N-glycosides and C-glycosides are used as class names for glycosylamines and for compounds having a glycosyl group attached to a hydrocarbyl group respectively. These terms are misnomers and should not be used. The preferred terms are glycosylamines and C-glycosyl compounds, respectively.
data.name: glycoside

data.definition: A biological role relating to the normal mechanisms and their interactions within a living system.
data.name: physiological role

data.definition: Compounds having the structure RC(=NR)NR<small><sub>2</sub></small>. The term is used as a suffix in systematic nomenclature to denote the ‒C(=NH)NH<small><sub>2</sub></small> group including its carbon atom.
data.name: carboxamidine

data.definition: Any  metabolite produced during a metabolic reaction in eukaryotes, the taxon that include members of the fungi, plantae and animalia kingdoms.
data.name: eukaryotic metabolite

data.definition: A gas in an atmosphere that absorbs and emits radiation within the thermal infrared range, so contributing to the 'greenhouse effect'.
data.name: greenhouse gas

data.definition: An erythromycin that consists of erythronolide A having 2,6-dideoxy-3-C-methyl-3-O-methyl-α-L-ribo-hexopyranosyl and 3,4,6-trideoxy-3-(dimethylamino)-β-D-xylo-hexopyranosyl residues attahced at positions 4 and 6 respectively.
data.name: erythromycin A

data.definition: An organic molecule or ion (usually a metal ion) that is required by an enzyme for its activity. It may be attached either loosely (coenzyme) or tightly (prosthetic group).
data.name: cofactor

data.definition: A glucan composed of unbranched chains of <small>D</small>-glucopyranose residues in α(1→4) glycosidic linkage. The number of repeated glucose subunits (n) is usually in the range of 300 to 3000, but can be many thousands. One of the two components of starch (the other, 70-80%, being amylopectin). Cf. linear maltodextrin, in which the chain length is typically between 3 and 17 glucose units.
data.name: amylose
